$comment: Where You Stand — the copy deck.
Every visitor-facing string is read from this file, by slot id. The author
writes every 'text'; the developer wires slots and never writes prose.
An empty slot is a slot still waiting, and the build says which.
The eighteen Tool 3 slots and their nine next steps are drafted in section
10 of the review. They are addressable by id alone, so wording can change
at any time without touching code.
Three rules, enforced by sim/tests/copy.test.js: no sentence may tell the
reader to buy, sell, switch, hold, redeem, stop or start anything; nothing
may reference a moment, so the copy never ages; and the words 'insider'

ABOUT-MAIN.text: This page runs the book's five questions on your own money. You enter what you paid in and took out; it fetches the fund's public NAV history, for any fund, including ones launched after this book was printed, and works everything out on your phone. Nothing you type leaves it. It does not rate funds, rank them, or tell you what to buy, sell or switch. It tells you where you stand and what to check next. Every sentence it shows is tied to a number it has just calculated, so the same figures will get the same sentence in ten years. It compares your fund with an index fund you could actually have bought, not with the index itself. Figures are before tax and exit load. It describes what has already happened and predicts nothing.
